To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the antigenic and immunogenic activities of tick-borne virus glycoprotein complexes are 10 to 15 times higher than those of whole virus when tested per microgram of viral protein; and (ii) the glycoprotein complex prepared after Triton-X solubilization has a protective activity in mice almost equal to that of whole virus.

(i) glycoprotein complexes can be prepared from tick-born encephalitis (TBE) virus by Triton X-10 solubilization and centrifugation into sucrose density gradients; (ii) these complexes are antigenically and immunogenetically equivalent to whole TBE virus; and (iii) the complexes are more antigenic than the whole virus in a radioimmunoassays, but they are less immunogenic than whole virus in the mouse protection test.
